Cognor Holding S.A. (formerly Cognor S.A.) is a Polish company headquartered in Poraj with its shares listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange since 1994. The Group's main activity is scrap metal collection and processing into steel wire, ready-made steel products, and other goods. As of September 30, 2025, the Group consisted of Cognor S.A., Cognor Holding S.A., Madrohut Sp. z o.o., JAP Industries s.r.o., Hutnik Kraków Sp. z o.o., ECOGNOR Sp. z o.o., WIZJA i WOLA Sp. z o.o., and Cognor Developer 1 Sp. z o.o.

Cognor Holding S.A. was established in 1991, acquired full control of Złomrex S.A. on January 27, 2006, and changed its name to Cognor Holding S.A. on November 29, 2016. On May 25, 2008, it acquired 88.13% ownership of Cognor Holding S.A., which held 50.9% voting rights in Cognor S.A. until January 27, 2006. On April 11, 2014, Cognor S.A. directly owned 23.60% of Madrohut Sp. z o.o., a joint venture with 25% ownership by Cognor Holding S.A.

On May 1, 2025, Cognor Holding S.A. established and acquired full control of Cognor Developer 1 Sp. z o.o. On January 1, 2023, it acquired JAP Industries s.r.o., Hutnik Kraków Sp. z o.o., ECOGNOR Sp. z o.o., and WIZJA i WOLA Sp. z o.o.

Cognor Holding S.A. (the "Company") is a Polish holding company with its registered office in Warsaw, Poland and its shares are listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange. The Company's consolidated financial statements for the nine months ended 30 September 2025 were prepared under the going concern assumption. The Group consists of Cognor Holding S.A., Cognor S.A., JAP Industries s.r.o., Hutnik Kraków Sp. z o.o., Ecognor Sp. z o.o., and Wizja i Wola Sp. z o.o. (the "Subsidiaries"). The Company is the Parent Company of the Group.

The consolidated financial statements for the nine months ended 30 September 2025 were prepared under the going concern assumption, which assumes that the Group will continue to operate as a going concern and that it has sufficient resources to meet its obligations as they become due. The preparation of these consolidated financial statements requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period. Actual results could differ from those estimates.

The Company's ability to continue as a going concernis dependent on its ability to generate sufficient cash flows from operations, obtain additional financing or complete an acquisition that would provide adequate resources for the Group to meet its obligations as they become due. The Company has been in discussions with banks regarding funding and is currently seeking payment of the second tranche of a credit facility from Bank Santander S.A., which is critical to the full settlement of the investment in Siemianowice Śląskie. Details of these negotiations are provided in Note 19.

Based on its analysis, current knowledge, and actions taken by management, the Company's Board of Directors confirms that the going concern assumption for the Group and the Parent Company is appropriate. Taking into account the above, the Company's Board of Directors has decided to prepare this condensed interim consolidated financial statements under the going concern basis in a manner consistent with the expected future developments.

In the opinion of management of Cognor Holding S.A., as at the date of preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, there are no material uncertainties related to events or conditions that may cast significant doubt on the Company's ability to continue as a going concern for a period of at least twelve months from the date of approval of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements.

The accounting policies applied in preparing this condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used in the preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024, which were prepared in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by the European Union. The Company's management has made significant estimates and assumptions in preparing these condensed interim consolidated financial statements.

The preparation of condensed interim consolidated financial statements requires management to make judgments, estimates, and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities at the date of the condensed interim consolidated financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period. Actual results could differ from those estimates.

Significant accounting estimates and judgements made by management in preparing these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used in the preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024, except for the impairment of assets (see Note 5).

Cognor Holding S.A. (WSE: COGN) is a Polish holding company with subsidiaries in the IT and software development sectors. The company's financial results for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 show a net loss of PLN47,915 million (USD11.3 million), compared to a net loss of PLN323,031 million (USD76.8 million) for the same period in 2024.

The company has issued convertible bonds with a nominal value of PLN100,000 thousand (USD23.9 million) and a maturity of up to seven years from issuance. The conversion ratio is 200 shares per bond, with a minimum conversion amount of one bond. The conversion price is PLN5.00 per share.

The company has also issued 20,000 ordinary shares with a nominal value of PLN1.50 each at an issue price of PLN5.00 per share. These shares are not subject to any special rights andwere issued as part of a conditional capital increase to grant bondholders the right to convert their bonds into shares.

The company has also granted its shareholders the right to subscribe for new shares in exchange for existing shares, with a conversion ratio of 200 shares per bond and a minimum subscription amount of one bond. The conversion price is PLN5.00 per share.

On March 8, 2023, the Board of Directors approved the issuance of 100,000 unsecured convertible bonds with a nominal value of PLN1,000 each and a total value of PLN100,000 thousand (USD23.9 million). The bonds have a maturity of up to seven years from issuance and are not backed by any collateral.

On March 28, 2025, Cognor Holding S.A., 4Workers Sp. z o.o. (now PS HoldCo Sp. z o.o.), and Value Fundusz Inwestycyjny Zamknięty signed an investment agreement under which the convertible bonds were sold to Value FIZ subject to certain conditions. Under the agreement, Value FIZ waived its right to redeem the bonds on maturity and committed to submit a conversion request by March 20, 2030, while Cognor Holding S.A. waived its right to early redemption of the bonds.

On May 28, 2025, the Board of Directors amended the Terms of Issue of Obligations, setting the interest rate at a fixed level of 10.5%. As part of implementing the conditions for the investment agreement sale of bonds from 4Workers Sp. z o.o. to Value FIZ, the transaction was completed.

As a result of this investment agreement and change in bond issue terms, Cognor Holding S.A. recognized a new compound instrument consisting of a capital component and a liability component. The capital component was recognized at PLN56,887 million (resulting from the obligation to convert bonds into shares on March 20, 2030) and presented in other capital, while the liability component (resulting from future interest flows) was recognized at PLN34,322 million. The company also recorded transaction costs of PLN8,791 million for the convertible bonds, split between the capital and liability components.

Details of the convertible bonds are described in note 10.

Despite the absence of financial covenants in Cognor's contracts, the following situation for the Group has direct implications on the company's financial position and ability to meet obligations:  
In recent years, the Group undertook many modernization projects with significant value. In 2023, we completed a furnace upgrade at Gliwice (EAF) worth nearly PLN100 million, including replacement of the main technological chain element. At Krakow in early 2024, we built a new furnace and replaced most elements of the rollingmill chain, adding an automated finishing section; we also installed a coil-winding line as a second branch, which was commissioned within weeks with success. Total investment exceeded PLN300 million. In Siemianowice Slaskie, we completed construction of Europe's most advanced U-shaped profile rolling mill to replace the closed-down Zawiercie facility, our largest investment at over PLN800 million; it is currently undergoing cold and hot line testing after successful completion. The first production trial was on 25 September when a piece was drawn from the furnace and sent to the rolling mill; we then tested various product groups, starting with round bars. We obtained approval for this entire range of products in parallel. Subsequent tests will cover equal-angle, unequal-angle, UPN tees, IPN double tees, flat bars,IPE double tees, UPE tees, and HE double tees; we expect to complete testing and obtain certification for all groups by year-end.  
Financing sources included own funds and external financing in the form of (i) PLN100 million exchangeable bonds issued in 2023 with a seven-year maturity (Exchangeable Bonds), (ii) unsecured ordinary bonds issued in 2024 at PLN240 million with five-year equal semi-annual installments (Bonds), and (iii) an investment loan with two-year utilization period and eight-year amortization schedule, paid in equal half-yearly installments and drawn from Santander Bank S.A. in 2021 for EUR30.5 million and PLN240 million, which was increased by a second trancheof EUR5.2 million and PLN120.4 million in 2024 (Investment Loan).

Due to investment works, individual plants had to suspend production; Gliwice's steelworks was idle for about half a year while Krakow's rolling mill was shut down for over a year. In both cases, the work schedule exceeded the plan and was followed by a lengthy startup period, especially at the main rolling line in Krakow. Construction in Siemianowice Slaskie also experienced delays, with the interval between closing the old Zawiercie facility in April 2024 and nearby production start-up having similar effects from our perspective: significant reduction of ordinary steel and construction products for the building sector.  
The modernization projects exceeded their budgets and especially schedules, causing costs of downtime related to these investments of PLN74.1 million in 2023 and PLN55.5 million in 2024; these amounts represent fixed costs incurred during periods when plants could not operate due to investment works. The cited expenditures, downtime costs, and difficult-to-estimate losses from reduced production and sales heavily affected our results over the past two years, with the prior year most strongly highlighting this burden as it was compounded by market downturn.  
The above circumstances resulted in a very significant deterioration of our profitability and cash flows, leading us to fail to meet minimum threshold levels for financial ratios specified in financing agreements at the endof Q3 2024, then year-end 2024, and first and second quarters of 2025. We approached cooperating financial institutions and received approvals for violations on balance dates ending Q3 and Q4 2024 as well as Q1 and Q2 2025. Expecting the problem to persist longer, we also requested permission to breach ratios at the end of subsequent quarters through year-end 2025; again, we obtained conditional consent from Santander Bank S.A., bondholders of Bonds, Alior Bank S.A., and mBank S.A., covering all institutions where we are obliged to maintain certain financial performance indicators.

Cognor Holding S.A. reported consolidated financial statements for the period from 1 January to 30 September 2025 (in thousands of Polish zlotys unless otherwise stated). The company and Santander Bank S.A. have agreed on a draft amendment to the investment credit agreement dated 21 December 2021 (Investment Credit) that would allow disbursement of the second tranche (approximately PLN 140 million) regardless of whether Cognor was in breach of two financial parameters currently included in financing agreements with Pekao Bank S.A. and an obligation issue agreement, which would also be introduced into the Investment Credit Agreement by Amendment No. 2. These financial parameters are EBITDA and operating cash flow for the period from the beginning of 2025 to the date of the tests, which were scheduled to occur at the end of each quarter in 2025. Since the operational cash flow parameter was breached as of mid-year 2025, Santander Bank S.A. began processing our credit application, which included elements previously agreed upon and consent for disbursement from the second tranche of Investment Credit despite the breach of financial parameters. Although our application to Santander Bank S.A. delays payment from the second tranche of Investment Credit, we aim to obtain maximum comfort in accessing the full amount of this tranche to settle all remaining investment obligations arising from the realization of the plant in Siemianowice Śląskie. On 6 October 2025, we received a positive credit decision from the bank and finalized the content of Amendment No. 2. We expect to sign it along with accompanying documentation and immediately submit an application for disbursement of funds from the second tranche of Investment Credit, which covers investment obligations arising from the construction of a rolling mill in Siemianowice Śląskie.

In this context, we assess the Group's ability tomeet its commitments in foreseeable perspective, including those resulting from completed investment projects, positively. Regardless of the success of talks with the Bank, the Management Board of Cognor Group convened an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders of Cognor Holding S.A. on 20 November 2025 to approve a capital increase. A successful issuance would allow for realization of certain additionalinvestment goals in subsequent periods, and until application of funds, the sums obtained will contribute to reducing net debt and improving liquidity margin.
